paper.title: Best-of-three-worlds Analysis for Linear Bandits with Follow-the-regularized-leader Algorithm

settings.name_in_paper: Linear bandits in adversarial environment (non-oblivious adversary)
unmapped: ||x||_2<=1 for all arms and ||theta_t||_2<=1; noise assumed zero in adversarial environment
settings.definition_quote: We denote by $D\subseteq \mathbb{R}^d$ the \textit{finite} arm set ... $D$ spans $\mathbb{R}^d$ and $\|x\|_2\leq 1$ ... we assume $\norm{\theta_t}_2 \le 1$ ... In this work, we consider the non-oblivious adversary

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic linear bandits with corruption level C (adversarial regime with self-bounding constraint)
unmapped: Corruption c_t is arbitrary (not necessarily linear in x_t), adaptive to history; C = sum_t |c_t|
settings.definition_quote: For the corrupted stochastic environment, it is also satisfied that $\theta_t=\theta$ for some \textit{unknown} $\theta$, but the learner now receives loss $\ell_t(x_t)=\left\langle x_t,\theta \right\rangle+\epsilon_t\left(x_t\right)+c_t$ ... let $C=\sum_{t=1}^T|c_t|$ be the corruption level

algorithms.name: FTRL for Linear Bandits (negative entropy regularizer + G-optimal design exploration)

source.label: thm:thmregret
source.quote: Choose $\psi_t(p) = -\beta_t H(p)$ and $\gamma_t = \min\sets{g(\pi)/\beta_t,1/2 }$ ... In the adversarial environment, regret can be upper bounded by $R(T) \le O\bracket{\sqrt{dT\ln T \ln(|D|T)}}$

results.notes: K = |D|. Learning rate uses ln T, so horizon known. Regret is expected pseudo-regret vs best arm in expectation.

source.label: thm:thmregret
source.quote: In the stochastic environment with corruption level $C$, the regret can be bounded by $R(T) \le O \bracket{\frac{ d\ln T \ln (|D|T) }{ \Delta_{\min}} + \sqrt{\frac{Cd\ln T \ln (|D|T)}{\Delta_{\min}}} }$

results.notes: Proof goes via the (Delta,C,T) self-bounding constraint; so also applies to that regime. C=0 gives the stochastic case. Noise boundedness implicitly assumed in proof (l_t^2<=1).
